payload.fact: LARAVEL 11/12 TRAP found 2026-08-15: $middleware->priority([...]) in bootstrap/app.php REPLACES the entire framework default priority list, it does not merge. Passing two classes left a 2-entry list with Authenticate absent, so a route middleware hoisted to position 0 ran BEFORE authentication and its abort(401) pre-empted the guest redirect. Symptom was a guest getting 401 instead of a redirect to /login, which reads like an auth-config problem, not a priority problem. Correct API: prependToPriorityList($before, $insert) / appendToPriorityList($after, $insert), which preserve the 13 defaults. Also note Illuminate\\Auth\\Middleware\\Authenticate is NOT in the default priority list, so it must be inserted explicitly if ordering against it matters. Guard with a test asserting index(Authenticate) < index(YourMiddleware) < index(SubstituteBindings)
payload.source: Reproduced and fixed in Brand New ERP P1; verified priority list went from 2 entries to 13 with correct ordering

payload.fact: LARAVEL 11/12 TRAP found 2026-08-15: framework AUTO-DISCOVERS listeners in app/Listeners (any class with a handle() method type-hinting an event). Adding an explicit Event::listen for the same event/listener pair registers it TWICE, so every side effect runs twice. In Brand New ERP P4 this silently reserved stock twice per order line - a duplicate-inventory bug that looked like a reservation logic error, not a wiring error. Fix: rely on auto-discovery OR disable it, never both. GUARD: assert Event::getListeners(YourEvent::class) has exactly the expected count; the guard was proven by planting the duplicate registration and confirming both the guard and the behavioural test fail
payload.source: Reproduced in Brand New ERP P4: 2 reservations for 1 order line; fixed and guarded

payload.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - reservation-based inventory with a provable invariant. stock.on_hand is signed (a real warehouse goes negative after a miscount; refusing to represent it turns a counting error into a 500). available = on_hand - reserved is DERIVED, never stored. Reserving changes only reserved; only commit changes on_hand and writes an append-only movement. Every on_hand change writes a movement carrying quantity_delta and a denormalised balance_after, so SUM(quantity_delta) == on_hand is a testable invariant per stock line. All mutations take a blocking SELECT FOR UPDATE on the stock row (not SKIP LOCKED - last-unit scarcity is queue-and-wait), and commit/release take their own lock so a reservation cannot be discharged twice
payload.source: Implemented in Brand New ERP P4; oversell reproduces on 3 of 3 runs when the lock is removed

payload.fact: POSTGRESQL CONSTRAINT found 2026-08-15: 'FOR UPDATE is not allowed with aggregate functions'. A sequence allocator written as Model::query()->where(...)->lockForUpdate()->max('sequence') is invalid SQL on Postgres and fails at runtime, not at analysis. Fix: lock the LAST ROW instead of the aggregate - orderByDesc('sequence')->lockForUpdate()->first() - then compute next in PHP, plus a retry on unique violation 23505 to cover the first-insert race where no row exists to lock
payload.source: Reproduced in Brand New ERP P5 attribution touch sequencing; fixed and 18 tests green

payload.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - attribution as its own polymorphic domain. attribution_touches is an append-only trail keyed (subject_type, subject_id, sequence); attributions holds ONE resolved row per subject and is polymorphic across Lead, Customer and Order. First touch wins for credit, but every touch is retained so last-touch and multi-touch reporting stay available and changing the credit rule is a rule change not a migration. An Order INHERITS from its lead (or the customer's own attribution) and is then FROZEN - re-attributing throws, because commission is paid on it. A converted customer inherits its lead's first touch. payload.fact: POSTGRESQL NULL-DISTINCTNESS TRAP found 2026-08-15: a UNIQUE index does NOT prevent duplicates when a participating column is NULL, because Postgres treats NULLs as distinct. A commission idempotency constraint on (company_id, order_id, order_item_id, recipient_user_id, plan_id, type) silently allowed unlimited duplicates for ORDER-LEVEL accruals where order_item_id is NULL - the exact rows the constraint existed to protect. Detected only because a test tried to insert a deliberate duplicate and no exception was thrown. FIX on PG15+: UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT (...). Verified: after the fix, removing the application-level idempotency check produces a UniqueConstraintViolationException instead of a duplicate row

payload.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - a commission that explains itself from data. Every accrual persists rule_version_id, basis_amount, rate_type, rate_applied and a calc_inputs JSONB holding the full margin decomposition (sales, cost, shipping, fees, allocated ad spend, each with a label and a human basis string). explain() then RENDERS that line rather than storing prose: 'Commission MYR 38.50 - Recipient: Ali (marketer) - Rule: "Facebook Campaign Margin" v1 (effective 2025-08-15) - 12% of MYR 320.80 - Sales MYR 1,000.00 - Cost MYR 520.00 - Shipping MYR 49.20 - Fees MYR 30.00 - Ads MYR 80.00 = MYR 320.80 - Order SO-00001 - Provisional'. Rule versions are immutable (DB trigger) and effective-dated, so a closed period can never be rewritten, and commissions are never deleted - a reversal is a contra entry with negated amount AND negated sources so the trail nets to zero
payload.source: Implemented in Brand New ERP P6; 23 tests covering all ten prior-art anti-patterns

payload.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - a minimal but real double-entry ledger for an SME ERP. accounts (asset/liability/equity/income/expense) + journal_entries + journal_lines. Balance is enforced three ways: the Ledger service refuses an unbalanced post with a readable message, a CHECK constraint requires total_debit = total_credit on the entry, and a per-line CHECK requires exactly one of debit or credit to be positive. journal_lines are append-only at the DB (UPDATE and DELETE both rejected) so corrections must be reversing entries. balanceOf() signs by account type and trialBalance() must always be zero - that single assertion catches almost every posting mistake. Commission flows through it properly: payable posts Dr Commission Expense / Cr Commission Payable, and the payout posts Dr Commission Payable / Cr Bank, so the payable account clears to zero
payload.source: Implemented in Brand New ERP P7; 19 tests including trial-balance assertions after issue, payment, void and payout

payload.fact: PHP TRAP repeated twice in one project (2026-08-15): enum instances CANNOT be used as array keys. foreach ([SomeEnum::A => X, SomeEnum::B => Y] as $k => $v) raises 'Cannot access offset of type SomeEnum on array' at runtime, not at analysis, and the message points at the foreach rather than at the literal. It bit Brand New ERP twice - once in P1 DataScopeTest and again in P5-P8 ReportingTest - because the map-literal reads naturally. FIX: use a list of pairs, foreach ([[SomeEnum::A, X], [SomeEnum::B, Y]] as [$k, $v]). Worth remembering because PHPStan does not catch it and the error surfaces far from the cause
payload.source: Two independent occurrences in Brand New ERP; both fixed with pair lists

payload.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - precomputed rollups verified by an INDEPENDENT live oracle. The rollup is built by SQL GROUP BY; the oracle recomputes the same figures by iterating orders in PHP with exact decimal Money arithmetic. Because the two paths share no code, comparing them is a real cross-check rather than a tautology - a planted bug (summing unit_cost without multiplying by quantity) is caught immediately. The comparison also proves freshness: rebuilding is idempotent (delete-then-insert per slice, asserted by rebuilding three times) and a cancelled order drops out on rebuild. The rollup slice key uses UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT so unattributed slices cannot silently duplicate
payload.source: Implemented in Brand New ERP P8; oracle catches a planted aggregation bug on the first run

payload.fact: OPERATIONAL TRAP found 2026-08-15 during a backup rehearsal: pg_dump REFUSES to dump a server newer than itself ('aborting because of server version mismatch'). On this machine the client on PATH is 14.18 while the server is 16.14, so the very first backup attempt failed outright. An unrehearsed backup plan would have discovered this during an incident. FIX: resolve a client binary whose MAJOR version matches the server before dumping - query 'show server_version_num', then look under /opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql@<major>/bin and /usr/lib/postgresql/<major>/bin, and verify with --version before use. Also refuse to write a dump under 1KB so an empty file is never mistaken for a backup. This is the THIRD time the client-vs-server version distinction has caused a defect on this project
payload.source: Reproduced in Brand New ERP P9; backup.sh and restore.sh now resolve the matching client

payload.fact: SECURITY FINDING 2026-08-15 Brand New ERP P9: Laravel 11/12 config/filesystems.php ships the local disk with 'serve' => true, which registers GET /storage/{path} AND PUT /storage/{path} with NO middleware whatsoever. On a system whose private disk holds business documents that is unauthenticated read AND write. It is invisible in route:list review unless you look at middleware, and no test catches it by default. FIX: set 'serve' => false on any private disk and serve documents through an authorised controller. GUARD: a test that fails if any route under storage/ has an empty middleware stack

payload.fact: MEASUREMENT TRAP 2026-08-15: an N+1 probe that compares query counts between a first and second request measures CACHE WARMING, not N+1. In Brand New ERP the audit screen showed 12 queries for 3 rows and 7 for 30 - the count went DOWN - because the first request primed the permission cache. Reading that as a pass or a fail would both have been wrong. FIX: issue one warm-up request before measuring, then compare steady-state counts at two data volumes within the SAME company and user

payload.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - landed cost that cannot double-count. Freight/duty/handling are recorded as goods_receipt_costs rows with an allocation rule (by_value, by_quantity, by_weight); the allocator apportions each pool across receipt lines and writes landed_unit_cost plus a landed_cost_basis JSONB holding every component, its share, its per-unit effect and a human explanation. The variant's average_cost is then RECOMPUTED FROM THE FULL RECEIPT HISTORY rather than maintained incrementally, which makes re-application idempotent by construction - no reversal bookkeeping, no drift. Order lines snapshot average_cost when it exists and record unit_cost_source so a margin figure can always say whether it rests on a real receipt or a typed guess
payload.source: Implemented in Brand New ERP after P9; 9 tests, both allocation modes proven distinct by mutation

payload.fact: REUSABLE PATTERN - a restore rehearsal that runs on a schedule. erp:backup dumps, prunes to a retention window and optionally copies offsite; erp:verify-backup restores the NEWEST dump into a scratch database, compares table/trigger/CHECK/foreign-key counts against the live schema, PROVES the restored copy still refuses a journal edit by inserting a real row and attempting to update it, drops the scratch database, and exits non-zero on any mismatch. Scheduled weekly, because a restore verified once decays. Three hardening details found by actually running it: a failed dump must delete its own partial file or a truncated file looks like a backup; filenames need a random suffix or two runs in the same second overwrite each other; and enabling offsite without a command must be a hard error
payload.source: Implemented and run in Brand New ERP; detected a genuine schema-drift mismatch 107/106 tables on an outdated dump
